mira: FYI nightly evals flagged a spike in regression rate for model-redwood-v2-quantized since we turned prefix cache on :thinking:

nightly-evals-bot: [2024-04-16T06:00Z] eval-run complete. Regression delta vs baseline: +4.7% (prompt-set: customer-support-20).

sophie: ugh. is this the determinism-on-change we've seen before with batching/caching?

dima: possibly. quick summary: we enabled prefix_cache_enabled=true + batching_window_ms=15 on the new infra for cost wins. Quantized int8 model on latest kernels.

mira: repro script shows nondeterministic generations when cache hit path triggers. when hit -> shorter latency but text diverges from golden. when miss -> matches golden.

sophie: can you paste the minimal repro and logs?

dima: paste below. minimal sequence that fails ~70% of runs on my box (seeded prompts).

```
# repro (python)
from redwood_api import Client
c = Client(model='redwood-v2-quantized')
prefix = "Support ticket: user can't login"
for i in range(20):
    out = c.generate(prefix=prefix, max_tokens=60)
    print(i, out.text[:80])
```

# observed log snippet
[2024-04-16T05:12:37Z] cache: lookup key=rv2q:pref_0x5a3f size=64 hit
[2024-04-16T05:12:37Z] runtime: apply_batch id=42 size=4 sequence_len=28
[2024-04-16T05:12:37Z] kvcache: restore k/v shape mismatch -> fallback=false (used cached kv)
[2024-04-16T05:12:37Z] decode: top_tokens differing from baseline at step 7

mira: note the kvcache restore line — shapes should not mismatch, but we still used cached kv when shapes didn't align. that smells like a cache key collision where prefix length hashing collided across templates.

sophie: did we namespace cache by model+quant_mode+prompt_template? I thought we added model+prefix_hash only.

dima: exactly — key format is currently `rv2q:pref_{prefix_hash}`. collision space small because prefix_hash is truncated to 32 bits for storage efficiency.

ops-bot: deployed config change: prefix_cache_enabled=true -> rolled at 2024-04-10 across canary fleet.

mira: experiments to run: 1) run nightly eval with prefix_cache disabled 2) increase prefix_hash to 128-bit 3) include model_version + quant_mode in key 4) run with batching_window_ms=0 (no batching) to confirm interaction.

sophie: I'll run 1 and 4 tonight. dima can you do 2+3 perf tradeoff assessment? if we switch to 128-bit keys we need storage-impact numbers.

dima: on it. early numbers: increasing hash to 128-bit increases cache index size ~+8% and memory +12% after accounting for metadata. hits stabilize better (fewer collisions).

mira: also want to check kernel path differences: cached kv restored might come from a different kernel (fp16 vs quant int8 packed layout) — need to include kernel_signature in cache key.

sophie: good catch. I've seen shape mismatch when sequence length bucketing differs between batches. might be a batching packing bug: the batcher reorders sequences and the KV restore uses wrong slot mapping when we reuse slots across batches.

dima: action items:
- dima: add model_version + quant_mode + kernel_sig to cache key, implement 128-bit prefix_hash, add a cache integrity assert that verifies tensor shapes before use (fail open -> miss). (ETA: EOD tomorrow)
- sophie: run nightly eval toggles (cache on/off, batching window 15/0) and post regression deltas. (ETA: next run)
- mira: triage prompt set failures, collect sample pairs (cached vs miss) and open a small eval watch with diff viewer. (ETA: today)

mira: sample pair (cached vs miss) below for prompt above:

CACHED: "... please try clearing your browser cookies and resetting the password link. if that fails, escalate to auth team."
MISS:   "... please verify you entered the correct email, then use the password reset flow. if it still fails, forward to account support."

mira: differences are subtle but change recommended next step -> can be bad for automation.

sophie: also check if quantization amplified the issue — quant errors + wrong kv shape can push logits across sampling threshold. run same test on fp16 model variant.

dima: will test fp16. if fp16 unaffected, we need to treat this as interaction: quantized kernels + cache rehydration bug. urgent P1 for rollbacks or hotfix on cache code.

nightly-evals-bot: [2024-04-16T07:00Z] queued: rerun eval on canary with cache_disabled and batching_window_ms=0 (run id rv2q-retest-20240416).

sophie: if rerun clears regression we should disable prefix cache on canary ASAP and push the key/fail-open assert fix to prod.

mira: agree. also add a gating check to rollout pipeline: if nightly regression delta > 1% for any customer prompt-set, auto halt rollout and alert oncall.

dima: noted. i'll also put a short-term mitigation: treat any cache-restore shape mismatch as a miss (don't use cached kv) — cheap and safe.

sophie: thanks — keep updates here. will post eval diffs when available. :thumbsup:
